title: Twenty years
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: The Anniversary as a week. Wood in the cafeteria for the first time since 1999, as a visitor, for a school-paper interview the strip never shows.

panels.composition: Small Wood High's cafeteria, 2017. Same room, new tables, a vending machine that takes cards. Three hundred kids facing one direction — toward their phones. WOOD in the doorway, a visitor badge on the flannel.

characters.pose: in the doorway with a visitor badge

image.prompt: a high school cafeteria seen from its doorway, hundreds of students all looking down at phones, a man in a flannel with a visitor badge standing in the door, razor-sharp ink
image.notes: Twenty years. One direction: down. The strip doesn't say it.

panels.composition: The serving line. A tray. Corn. A LUNCH LADY — a different one; the first retired. She looks up. That's the difference.

balloons.text: You're the one from the paper. The old paper.

image.prompt: a man holding out a tray at a cafeteria serving line as a lunch lady ladles corn and actually looks up at him

panels.composition: The long table. Wood at the end with his corn. Three kids at the far end, one drawing on a napkin, one reading, one with a phone. He draws them without their noticing.

characters.pose: three kids far down the table

image.prompt: a long cafeteria table with a man alone at one end drawing and three teenagers far at the other end: one drawing on a napkin, one reading a paperback, one on a phone, no words
image.notes: #1's last panel, with a phone in it. The kid on the napkin is the one he draws.

panels.composition: The cafeteria from the door, later, empty. The trays stacked. Wood gone. The strip's twentieth-anniversary panel is the room without him.

image.prompt: an empty high school cafeteria seen from the doorway after lunch, trays stacked, nobody in it, clean ink, no words

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; the pup's weight learned; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: dailies: ink and one tone. Sundays: gray-green, fog, rust, bruised dusk

notes: Twenty. The cafeteria, the corn, the napkin kid. The interview never shown.
